segs.p: “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekanīvaraṇampi samanupassāmi yena nīvaraṇena nivutā pajā dīgharattaṁ sandhāvanti saṁsaranti yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, avijjānīvaraṇaṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I do not see a single shroud, shrouded by which people wander and transmigrate for a long time like the shroud of ignorance.

segs.p: Avijjānīvaraṇena hi, bhikkhave, nivutā pajā dīgharattaṁ sandhāvanti saṁsarantī”ti.
segs.e: Shrouded by ignorance, people wander and transmigrate for a long time.”
Those who have given up delusion,
the root is not found in them.”

segs.e: “Mendicants, I do not see a single fetter, fettered by which people wander and transmigrate for a long time like the fetter of craving.

as they transmigrate on this long journey.

rid of craving, free of grasping,

segs.p: “Sekhassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno appattamānasassa anuttaraṁ yogakkhemaṁ patthayamānassa viharato ajjhattikaṁ aṅganti karitvā nāññaṁ ekaṅgampi samanupassāmi yaṁ evaṁ bahūpakāraṁ yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, yoniso manasikāro.
segs.e: “Taking into account interior factors, mendicants, I do not see a single one that is so very helpful as rational application of mind for a trainee mendicant who hasn’t achieved their heart’s desire, but lives aspiring to the supreme sanctuary from the yoke.

segs.p: Yoniso, bhikkhave, bhikkhu manasi karonto akusalaṁ pajahati, kusalaṁ bhāvetī”ti.
segs.e: A mendicant rationally applying the mind gives up the unskillful and develops the skillful.”

segs.p: Ayampi attho vutto bhagavatā, iti me sutanti.
segs.e: This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.

segs.p: “Sekhassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno appattamānasassa anuttaraṁ yogakkhemaṁ patthayamānassa viharato bāhiraṁ aṅganti karitvā nāññaṁ ekaṅgampi samanupassāmi yaṁ evaṁ bahūpakāraṁ yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, kalyāṇamittatā.
segs.e: “Taking into account exterior factors, mendicants, I do not see a single one that is so very helpful as good friendship for a trainee mendicant who hasn’t achieved their heart’s desire, but lives aspiring to the supreme sanctuary from the yoke.

segs.p: Kalyāṇamitto, bhikkhave, bhikkhu akusalaṁ pajahati, kusalaṁ bhāvetī”ti.
segs.e: A mendicant who has good friends gives up the unskillful and develops the skillful.”

segs.p: Ayampi attho vutto bhagavatā, iti me sutanti.

segs.p: “Ekadhammo, bhikkhave, loke uppajjamāno uppajjati bahujanāhitāya bahujanāsukhāya bahuno janassa anatthāya ahitāya dukkhāya devamanussānaṁ.
segs.e: “One thing, mendicants, arises in the world for the detriment and unhappiness of the people, against the people, for the harm, detriment, and suffering of gods and humans.

segs.p: Saṅghe kho pana, bhikkhave, bhinne aññamaññaṁ bhaṇḍanāni ceva honti, aññamaññaṁ paribhāsā ca honti, aññamaññaṁ parikkhepā ca honti, aññamaññaṁ pariccajanā ca honti.
segs.e: When the Saṅgha is split, they argue, insult, block, and forsake each other.

segs.p: Tattha appasannā ceva nappasīdanti, pasannānañca ekaccānaṁ aññathattaṁ hotī”ti.
segs.e: This doesn’t inspire confidence in those without it, and it causes some with confidence to change their minds.”
in a place of loss, in hell.
Taking a stand against the teaching,
favoring factions, they ruin their sanctuary.
After causing schism in a harmonious Saṅgha,
they burn in hell for an eon.”

segs.p: Ayampi attho vutto bhagavatā, iti me sutanti.
segs.e: This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.

segs.p: “Ekadhammo, bhikkhave, loke uppajjamāno uppajjati bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya bahuno janassa atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṁ.
segs.e: “One thing, mendicants, arises in the world for the welfare and happiness of the people, for the people, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.

segs.p: Saṅghe kho pana, bhikkhave, samagge na ceva aññamaññaṁ bhaṇḍanāni honti, na ca aññamaññaṁ paribhāsā honti, na ca aññamaññaṁ parikkhepā honti, na ca aññamaññaṁ pariccajanā honti.
segs.e: When the Saṅgha is in harmony, they don’t argue, insult, block, or forsake each other.

segs.p: Tattha appasannā ceva pasīdanti, pasannānañca bhiyyobhāvo hotī”ti.
segs.e: This inspires confidence in those without it, and increases confidence in those who have it.”
as is support for those in harmony.
Taking a stand on the teaching,
favoring harmony, they ruin no sanctuary.
After creating harmony in the Saṅgha,
they rejoice in heaven for an eon.”

segs.p: Ayampi attho vutto bhagavatā, iti me sutanti.
segs.e: This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.

segs.p: “Idhāhaṁ, bhikkhave, ekaccaṁ puggalaṁ paduṭṭhacittaṁ evaṁ cetasā ceto paricca pajānāmi:
segs.e: “Mendicants, when I’ve comprehended the mind of an individual whose mind is corrupted, I understand:

segs.p: ‘imamhi cāyaṁ samaye puggalo kālaṁ kareyya yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ niraye’.
segs.e: ‘If this individual were to die right now, they would be placed in hell as if delivered there.’

segs.p: Cetopadosahetu kho pana, bhikkhave, evam’idhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjantī”ti.
segs.e: Corruption of mind is the reason why some sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.”
were to die at this time,
That sort is cast down as surely
as if they’d been carried off and put there.
For corruption of mind is the reason
sentient beings go to a bad place.”

segs.p: Ayampi attho vutto bhagavatā, iti me sutanti.
segs.e: This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.

segs.p: “Idhāhaṁ, bhikkhave, ekaccaṁ puggalaṁ pasannacittaṁ evaṁ cetasā ceto paricca pajānāmi:
segs.e: “Mendicants, when I’ve comprehended the mind of an individual whose mind is pure, I understand:

segs.p: ‘imamhi cāyaṁ samaye puggalo kālaṁ kareyya yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ sagge’.
segs.e: ‘If this individual were to die right now, they would be placed in heaven as if delivered there.’

segs.p: Cetopasādahetu kho pana, bhikkhave, evam’idhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapajjantī”ti.
segs.e: Purity of mind is the reason why some sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.”
were to die at this time,
That sort is raised up as surely
as if they’d been carried and put there.
For purity of mind is the reason
sentient beings go to a good place.”

segs.p: Ayampi attho vutto bhagavatā, iti me sutanti.
segs.e: This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.

segs.p: Sukhassetaṁ, bhikkhave, adhivacanaṁ iṭṭhassa kantassa piyassa manāpassa yadidaṁ puññāni.
segs.e: For ‘good deeds’ is a term for happiness, for what is likable, desirable, and agreeable.

segs.p: Abhijānāmi kho panāhaṁ, bhikkhave, dīgharattaṁ katānaṁ puññānaṁ iṭṭhaṁ kantaṁ piyaṁ manāpaṁ vipākaṁ paccanubhūtaṁ.
segs.e: I recall undergoing for a long time the likable, desirable, and agreeable results of good deeds performed over a long time.

segs.p: Satta vassāni mettacittaṁ bhāvetvā satta saṁvaṭṭavivaṭṭakappe nayimaṁ lokaṁ punarāgamāsiṁ.
segs.e: Having developed a mind of love for seven years, for seven eons of the cosmos contracting and expanding I didn’t return to this world again.

segs.p: Saṁvaṭṭamāne sudaṁ, bhikkhave, kappe ābhassarūpago homi;
segs.e: As the eon contracted I went to the realm of sublime luminosity.
As it expanded I was reborn in an empty mansion of divinity.

segs.p: Tatra sudaṁ, bhikkhave, brahmā homi mahābrahmā abhibhū anabhibhūto aññadatthudaso vasavattī.
segs.e: There I was the Divinity, the Great Divinity, the vanquisher, the unvanquished, the universal seer, the wielder of power.

segs.p: Chattiṁsakkhattuṁ kho panāhaṁ, bhikkhave, sakko ahosiṁ devānamindo;
segs.e: I was Sakka, lord of gods, thirty-six times.

segs.p: anekasatakkhattuṁ rājā ahosiṁ cakkavattī dhammiko dhammarājā cāturanto vijitāvī janapadatthāvariyappatto sattaratanasamannāgato.
segs.e: Many hundreds of times I was a king, a wheel-turning monarch, a just and principled king. My dominion extended to all four sides, I achieved stability in the country, and I possessed the seven treasures.

segs.p: ‘kissa nu kho me idaṁ kammassa phalaṁ, kissa kammassa vipāko, yenāhaṁ etarahi evaṁmahiddhiko evaṁmahānubhāvo’ti?
segs.e: ‘Of what deed of mine is this the fruit and result, that I am now so mighty and powerful?’

segs.p: ‘tiṇṇaṁ kho me idaṁ kammānaṁ phalaṁ, tiṇṇaṁ kammānaṁ vipāko, yenāhaṁ etarahi evaṁmahiddhiko evaṁmahānubhāvoti, seyyathidaṁ—
segs.e: ‘It is the fruit and result of three kinds of deeds:

segs.p: Ayampi attho vutto bhagavatā, iti me sutanti.
segs.e: This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.

segs.p: “Ekadhammo, bhikkhave, bhāvito bahulīkato ubho atthe samadhigayha tiṭṭhati—
segs.e: “This one thing, mendicants, when developed and cultivated, secures equal benefits for both
this life and lives to come.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, bhikkhave, ekadhammo bhāvito bahulīkato ubho atthe samadhigayha tiṭṭhati—
segs.e: This is the one thing that, when developed and cultivated, secures equal benefits for both
this life and lives to come.”
they are said to be astute.”

segs.p: Ayampi attho vutto bhagavatā, iti me sutanti.
segs.e: This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.

segs.p: “Ekapuggalassa, bhikkhave, kappaṁ sandhāvato saṁsarato siyā evaṁ mahā aṭṭhikaṅkalo aṭṭhipuñjo aṭṭhirāsi yathāyaṁ vepullo pabbato, sace saṁhārako assa, sambhatañca na vinasseyyā”ti.
segs.e: “Mendicants, one individual roaming and transmigrating for an eon would amass a heap of bones the size of this Mount Vepulla, if they were gathered together and not lost.”
“If the bones of a single individual
for a single eon were gathered up,
they’d make a pile the size of a mountain:
And this is declared to be
in the Mountainfold of the Magadhans.
that leads to the stilling of suffering.
After roaming on seven times at most,
with the ending of all fetters.”

segs.p: Ayampi attho vutto bhagavatā, iti me sutanti.
segs.e: This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.

segs.p: “Ekadhammaṁ atītassa, bhikkhave, purisapuggalassa nāhaṁ tassa kiñci pāpakammaṁ akaraṇīyanti vadāmi.
segs.e: “Mendicants, for an individual person who transgresses in one thing, there is no bad deed they would not do, I say.
It is this: telling a deliberate lie.”
there is no evil they would not do.”

segs.p: Ayampi attho vutto bhagavatā, iti me sutanti.
segs.e: This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.

segs.p: “Evañce, bhikkhave, sattā jāneyyuṁ dānasaṁvibhāgassa vipākaṁ yathāhaṁ jānāmi, na adatvā bhuñjeyyuṁ, na ca nesaṁ maccheramalaṁ cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭheyya.
segs.e: “Mendicants, if sentient beings only knew, as I do, the fruit of giving and sharing, they would not eat without first giving, and the stain of stinginess would not occupy their minds.

segs.p: Yopi nesaṁ assa carimo ālopo carimaṁ kabaḷaṁ, tatopi na asaṁvibhajitvā bhuñjeyyuṁ, sace nesaṁ paṭiggāhakā assu.
segs.e: They would not eat without sharing even their last mouthful, their last morsel, so long as there was someone to receive it.

segs.p: Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, sattā na evaṁ jānanti dānasaṁvibhāgassa vipākaṁ yathāhaṁ jānāmi, tasmā adatvā bhuñjanti, maccheramalañca nesaṁ cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhatī”ti.
segs.e: It is because sentient beings do not know, as I do, the fruit of giving and sharing, that they eat without first giving, and the stain of stinginess occupies their minds.”
as taught by the great seer!
Rid of the stain of stinginess,
they would duly give to the noble ones,
where a gift is very fruitful.
to those worthy of a religious donation,
after passing from the human realm,
And when they have arrived there in heaven,
they enjoy all the pleasures they desire.

segs.p: Ayampi attho vutto bhagavatā, iti me sutanti.
segs.e: This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.

segs.p: “Yāni kānici, bhikkhave, opadhikāni puññakiriyavatthūni sabbāni tāni mettāya cetovimuttiyā kalaṁ nāgghanti soḷasiṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, of all the grounds for making worldly merit, none are worth a sixteenth part of the heart’s release by love.

segs.p: Mettāyeva tāni cetovimutti adhiggahetvā bhāsate ca tapate ca virocati ca.
segs.e: Surpassing them, the heart’s release by love shines and glows and dazzles.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, yā kāci tārakarūpānaṁ pabhā sabbā tā candiyā pabhāya kalaṁ nāgghanti soḷasiṁ, candapabhāyeva tā adhiggahetvā bhāsate ca tapate ca virocati ca;
segs.e: It’s like how the radiance of all the stars is not worth a sixteenth part of the moon’s radiance. Surpassing them, the moon’s radiance shines and glows and dazzles.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, yāni kānici opadhikāni puññakiriyavatthūni sabbāni tāni mettāya cetovimuttiyā kalaṁ nāgghanti soḷasiṁ, mettāyeva tāni cetovimutti adhiggahetvā bhāsate ca tapate ca virocati ca.
segs.e: In the same way, of all the grounds for making worldly merit, none are worth a sixteenth part of the heart’s release by love. Surpassing them, the heart’s release by love shines and glows and dazzles.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, vassānaṁ pacchime māse saradasamaye viddhe vigatavalāhake deve ādicco nabhaṁ abbhussakkamāno sabbaṁ ākāsagataṁ tamagataṁ abhivihacca bhāsate ca tapate ca virocati ca;
segs.e: It’s like the last month of the rainy season, in autumn, when the heavens are sunny and cloudless. And as the sun is rising to the firmament, having dispelled all the darkness of space, it shines and glows and dazzles.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, yāni kānici opadhikāni puññakiriyavatthūni sabbāni tāni mettāya cetovimuttiyā kalaṁ nāgghanti soḷasiṁ, mettāyeva tāni cetovimutti adhiggahetvā bhāsate ca tapate ca virocati ca.
segs.e: In the same way, of all the grounds for making worldly merit, none are worth a sixteenth part of the heart’s release by love. Surpassing them, the heart’s release by love shines and glows and dazzles.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, rattiyā paccūsasamayaṁ osadhitārakā bhāsate ca tapate ca virocati ca;
segs.e: It’s like how, at the crack of dawn, the morning star shines and glows and dazzles.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, yāni kānici opadhikāni puññakiriyavatthūni sabbāni tāni mettāya cetovimuttiyā kalaṁ nāgghanti soḷasiṁ, mettāyeva tāni cetovimutti adhiggahetvā bhāsate ca tapate ca virocati cā”ti.
segs.e: In the same way, of all the grounds for making worldly merit, none are worth a sixteenth part of the heart’s release by love. Surpassing them, the heart’s release by love shines and glows and dazzles.”
Loving just one creature with a hateless heart
a noble one creates abundant merit.
The royal potentates conquered this land
the sacrifices of the ‘casting of the yoke-pin’, <j>the ‘royal soma drinking’, and the ‘unimpeded’.
These are not worth a sixteenth part
of the mind developed with love,
as starlight cannot rival the moon.
Don’t kill or cause others to kill,
don’t conquer or encourage others to conquer,
with love for all living creatures—
you’ll have no enmity for anyone.”

segs.p: Ayampi attho vutto bhagavatā, iti me sutanti.
segs.e: This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.

segs.p: “Dvīhi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu diṭṭheva dhamme dukkhaṁ viharati savighātaṁ saupāyāsaṁ sapariḷāhaṁ;
segs.e: “Mendicants, when a mendicant has two qualities they live unhappily in this very life—with distress, anguish, and fever—

segs.p: kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā duggati pāṭikaṅkhā.
segs.e: and when the body breaks up, after death, they can expect a bad rebirth.

segs.p: Indriyesu aguttadvāratāya ca, bhojane amattaññutāya ca.
segs.e: Not guarding the sense doors and eating too much.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, dvīhi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu diṭṭheva dhamme dukkhaṁ viharati savighātaṁ saupāyāsaṁ sapariḷāhaṁ;
segs.e: When a mendicant possesses these two qualities they live unhappily in this very life—with distress, anguish, and fever—

segs.p: kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā duggati pāṭikaṅkhā”ti.
segs.e: and when the body breaks up, after death, they can expect a bad rebirth.”
such a person lives in suffering.”

segs.p: Ayampi attho vutto bhagavatā, iti me sutanti.
segs.e: This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.

segs.p: “Dvīhi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu diṭṭheva dhamme sukhaṁ viharati avighātaṁ anupāyāsaṁ apariḷāhaṁ;
segs.e: “Mendicants, when a mendicant has two qualities they live happily in this very life—without distress, anguish, and fever—

segs.p: kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugati pāṭikaṅkhā.
segs.e: and when the body breaks up, after death, they can expect a good rebirth.

segs.p: Indriyesu guttadvāratāya ca, bhojane mattaññutāya ca.
segs.e: Guarding the sense doors and moderation in eating.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, dvīhi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu diṭṭheva dhamme sukhaṁ viharati avighātaṁ anupāyāsaṁ apariḷāhaṁ;
segs.e: When a mendicant possesses these two qualities they live happily in this very life—without distress, anguish, and fever—

segs.p: kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugati pāṭikaṅkhā”ti.
segs.e: and when the body breaks up, after death, they can expect a good rebirth.”
such a person lives in happiness.”

segs.p: Ayampi attho vutto bhagavatā, iti me sutanti.
segs.e: This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco akatakalyāṇo hoti, akatakusalo, akatabhīruttāṇo, katapāpo, kataluddo, katakibbiso.
segs.e: It’s when someone hasn’t done good and skillful things that keep them safe, but has done bad things, violence and sin.

segs.p: So ‘akataṁ me kalyāṇan’tipi tappati, ‘kataṁ me pāpan’tipi tappati.
segs.e: Thinking, ‘I haven’t done good things’, they’re mortified. Thinking, ‘I have done bad things’, they’re mortified.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, dve dhammā tapanīyā”ti.
segs.e: These are the two things that are mortifying.”
when their body breaks up, that witless person

segs.p: Ayampi attho vutto bhagavatā, iti me sutanti.
segs.e: This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.
“These two things, mendicants, are not mortifying.

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco katakalyāṇo hoti, katakusalo, katabhīruttāṇo, akatapāpo, akataluddo, akatakibbiso.
segs.e: It’s when someone has done good and skillful things that keep them safe, but has not done bad things, violence and sin.

segs.p: So ‘kataṁ me kalyāṇan’tipi na tappati, ‘akataṁ me pāpan’tipi na tappati.
segs.e: Thinking, ‘I have done good things’, they’re not mortified. Thinking, ‘I haven’t done bad things’, they’re not mortified.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, dve dhammā atapanīyā”ti.
segs.e: These are the two things that are not mortifying.”
when their body breaks up, that wise person

segs.p: Ayampi attho vutto bhagavatā, iti me sutanti.
segs.e: This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.

segs.p: “Dvīhi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato puggalo yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ niraye.
segs.e: “Mendicants, an individual with two qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.

segs.p: Pāpakena ca sīlena, pāpikāya ca diṭṭhiyā.
Imehi kho, bhikkhave, dvīhi dhammehi samannāgato puggalo yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ niraye”ti.
segs.e: An individual with these two qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.”
when their body breaks up, that witless person

segs.p: Ayampi attho vutto bhagavatā, iti me sutanti.
segs.e: This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.

segs.p: “Dvīhi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato puggalo yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ sagge.
segs.e: “Mendicants, an individual with two qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.

segs.p: Bhaddakena ca sīlena, bhaddikāya ca diṭṭhiyā.
Imehi kho, bhikkhave, dvīhi dhammehi samannāgato puggalo yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ sagge”ti.
segs.e: An individual with these two qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.”
when their body breaks up, that wise person

segs.p: Ayampi attho vutto bhagavatā, iti me sutanti.
segs.e: This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.

segs.p: “Anātāpī, bhikkhave, bhikkhu anottāpī abhabbo sambodhāya, abhabbo nibbānāya, abhabbo anuttarassa yogakkhemassa adhigamāya.
segs.e: “Mendicants, without being keen and prudent a mendicant can’t achieve awakening, extinguishment, and the supreme sanctuary from the yoke.

segs.p: Ātāpī ca kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ottāpī bhabbo sambodhāya, bhabbo nibbānāya, bhabbo anuttarassa yogakkhemassa adhigamāyā”ti.
segs.e: But if a mendicant is keen and prudent they can achieve awakening, extinguishment, and the supreme sanctuary from the yoke.”
One who is mindful, alert, meditative,
having cut the fetter of birth and old age,
would experience supreme awakening <j>in this very life.”

segs.p: Ayampi attho vutto bhagavatā, iti me sutanti.
segs.e: This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.

segs.p: “Nayidaṁ, bhikkhave, brahmacariyaṁ vussati janakuhanatthaṁ, na janalapanatthaṁ, na lābhasakkārasilokānisaṁsatthaṁ, na ‘iti maṁ jano jānātū’ti.
segs.e: “Mendicants, this spiritual life is not lived for the sake of fawning or flattering people, nor for the benefit of possessions, honor, or popularity, nor thinking, ‘So let people know about me!’

segs.p: Atha kho idaṁ, bhikkhave, brahmacariyaṁ vussati saṁvaratthañceva pahānatthañcā”ti.
segs.e: This spiritual life is lived for the sake of restraint and giving up.”
but for the sake of restraint and giving up,
and because its objective is extinguishment.
This is the path followed by the great souls,
as it was taught by the Buddha

segs.p: Ayampi attho vutto bhagavatā, iti me sutanti.
segs.e: This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.

segs.p: “Nayidaṁ, bhikkhave, brahmacariyaṁ vussati janakuhanatthaṁ, na janalapanatthaṁ, na lābhasakkārasilokānisaṁsatthaṁ, na ‘iti maṁ jano jānātū’ti.
segs.e: “Mendicants, this spiritual life is not lived for the sake of fawning or flattering people, nor for the benefit of possessions, honor, or popularity, nor thinking, ‘So let people know about me!’

segs.p: Atha kho idaṁ, bhikkhave, brahmacariyaṁ vussati abhiññatthañceva pariññatthañcā”ti.
segs.e: This spiritual life is lived for the sake of direct knowledge and complete understanding.”
but for the sake of insight and understanding,
and because it culminates in extinguishment.
This is the path followed by the great souls,
as it was taught by the Buddha

segs.p: Ayampi attho vutto bhagavatā, iti me sutanti.
segs.e: This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.

segs.p: “Dvīhi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu diṭṭheva dhamme sukhasomanassabahulo viharati, yoni cassa āraddhā hoti āsavānaṁ khayāya.
segs.e: “Mendicants, when a mendicant has two qualities they’re full of joy and happiness in this very life, and they have laid the groundwork for ending the defilements.

segs.p: Saṁvejanīyesu ṭhānesu saṁvejanena, saṁviggassa ca yoniso padhānena.
segs.e: Being inspired at inspiring places, and making a suitable effort when inspired.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, dvīhi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu diṭṭheva dhamme sukhasomanassabahulo viharati, yoni cassa āraddhā hoti āsavānaṁ khayāyā”ti.
segs.e: When a mendicant possesses these two qualities they’re full of joy and happiness in this very life, and they have laid the groundwork for ending the defilements.”
an astute person should be inspired;
A mendicant living like this, with keen energy,

segs.p: Ayampi attho vutto bhagavatā, iti me sutanti.
segs.e: This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.

segs.p: “Tathāgataṁ, bhikkhave, arahantaṁ sammāsambuddhaṁ dve vitakkā bahulaṁ samudācaranti—
segs.e: “Two thoughts, mendicants, often occur to the Realized One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha:
the thought of sanctuary, and that of seclusion.
The Realized One loves kindness and delights in it,

segs.p: Tamenaṁ, bhikkhave, tathāgataṁ abyāpajjhārāmaṁ abyāpajjharataṁ eseva vitakko bahulaṁ samudācarati:
segs.e: so this thought often occurs to him:

segs.p: ‘imāyāhaṁ iriyāya na kañci byābādhemi tasaṁ vā thāvaraṁ vā’ti.
segs.e: ‘Through this behavior, I shall not hurt any creature firm or frail.’
The Realized One loves seclusion and delights in it,

segs.p: Tamenaṁ, bhikkhave, tathāgataṁ pavivekārāmaṁ pavivekarataṁ eseva vitakko bahulaṁ samudācarati:
segs.e: so this thought often occurs to him:
‘What is unskillful has been given up.’

segs.p: Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, tumhepi abyāpajjhārāmā viharatha abyāpajjharatā.
segs.e: So, mendicants, you too should love kindness and delight in it,

segs.p: Tesaṁ vo, bhikkhave, tumhākaṁ abyāpajjhārāmānaṁ viharataṁ abyāpajjharatānaṁ eseva vitakko bahulaṁ samudācarissati:
segs.e: then this thought will often occur to you:

segs.p: ‘imāya mayaṁ iriyāya na kañci byābādhema tasaṁ vā thāvaraṁ vā’ti.
segs.e: ‘Through this behavior, I shall not hurt any creature firm or frail.’
You too should love seclusion and delight in it,

segs.p: Tesaṁ vo, bhikkhave, tumhākaṁ pavivekārāmānaṁ viharataṁ pavivekaratānaṁ eseva vitakko bahulaṁ samudācarissati:
segs.e: then this thought will often occur to you:
‘What is unskillful? What is not given up? What should I give up?’”
the Realized One, the bearer of the unbearable:
first mentioned was thought of sanctuary,
then the second made clear was seclusion.
Dispeller of darkness, the great seer has crossed over:
the attained, the master, the undefiled.
In the midst of it all, <j>he is freed in the ending of craving;
that sage bears his final body.
He has disposed of Māra, I declare, <j>and gone beyond old age.
Standing high on a rocky mountain,
you can see the people all around.
In just the same way, the All-seer, so intelligent,
having ascended the Temple of Truth,
rid of sorrow, looks upon the people
swamped with sorrow, <j>overcome by rebirth and old age.”

segs.p: Ayampi attho vutto bhagavatā, iti me sutanti.
segs.e: This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.

segs.p: “Tathāgatassa, bhikkhave, arahato sammāsambuddhassa dve dhammadesanā pariyāyena bhavanti.
segs.e: “Mendicants, the Realized One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha has two approaches to teaching Dhamma.
this is the first approach to teaching Dhamma.

segs.p: ‘pāpaṁ pāpakato disvā tattha nibbindatha virajjatha vimuccathā’ti—
segs.e: ‘Having seen evil as evil, be disillusioned, dispassionate, and freed from it’—
this is the second approach to teaching Dhamma.

segs.p: Tathāgatassa, bhikkhave, arahato sammāsambuddhassa imā dve dhammadesanā pariyāyena bhavantī”ti.
segs.e: The Realized One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha has these two approaches to teaching Dhamma.”
used by the Realized One, the Buddha,
Then, with a mind free of desire,
you’ll make an end of suffering.”

segs.p: Ayampi attho vutto bhagavatā, iti me sutanti.
segs.e: This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.

segs.p: “Avijjā, bhikkhave, pubbaṅgamā akusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ samāpattiyā anvadeva ahirikaṁ anottappaṁ;
segs.e: “Mendicants, ignorance leads the attainment of unskillful qualities, with lack of conscience and prudence following along.

segs.p: vijjā ca kho, bhikkhave, pubbaṅgamā kusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ samāpattiyā anvadeva hirottappan”ti.
segs.e: Knowledge leads the attainment of skillful qualities, with conscience and prudence following along.”
in this world or the next,
Since one of corrupt wishes is
which sends them to a place of loss.

segs.p: Ayampi attho vutto bhagavatā, iti me sutanti.
segs.e: This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.

segs.p: “Te, bhikkhave, sattā suparihīnā ye ariyāya paññāya parihīnā.
segs.e: “Those sentient beings are truly bereft, mendicants, who are bereft of noble wisdom.

segs.p: Te diṭṭheva dhamme dukkhaṁ viharanti savighātaṁ saupāyāsaṁ sapariḷāhaṁ;
segs.e: They live unhappily in this very life—with distress, anguish, and fever—

segs.p: kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā duggati pāṭikaṅkhā.
segs.e: and when the body breaks up, after death, they can expect a bad rebirth.

segs.p: Te, bhikkhave, sattā aparihīnā ye ariyāya paññāya aparihīnā.
segs.e: Those sentient beings are not bereft who are not bereft of noble wisdom.

segs.p: Te diṭṭheva dhamme sukhaṁ viharanti avighātaṁ anupāyāsaṁ apariḷāhaṁ;
segs.e: In this very life they’re happy—free of distress, anguish, and fever—

segs.p: kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugati pāṭikaṅkhā”ti.
segs.e: and when the body breaks up, after death, they can expect a good rebirth.”
Wisdom is best in the world,
the ending of rebirth and continued existence.

segs.p: Ayampi attho vutto bhagavatā, iti me sutanti.
segs.e: This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.
“These two bright things, mendicants, protect the world.

segs.p: Ime ce, bhikkhave, dve sukkā dhammā lokaṁ na pāleyyuṁ, nayidha paññāyetha mātāti vā mātucchāti vā mātulānīti vā ācariyabhariyāti vā garūnaṁ dārāti vā.
segs.e: If these two bright things did not protect the world, there would be no recognition of the status of mother, aunts, or wives and partners of tutors and respected people.

segs.p: Sambhedaṁ loko agamissa yathā ajeḷakā kukkuṭasūkarā soṇasiṅgālā.
segs.e: The world would become dissolute, like goats and sheep, chickens and pigs, and hounds and jackals.

segs.p: Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, ime dve sukkā dhammā lokaṁ pālenti tasmā paññāyati mātāti vā mātucchāti vā mātulānīti vā ācariyabhariyāti vā garūnaṁ dārāti vā”ti.
segs.e: But because the two bright things protect the world, there is recognition of the status of mother, aunts, and wives and partners of tutors and respected people.”
and fare on in birth and death.
Those in whom conscience and prudence
being at peace, they will not be reborn again.”

segs.p: Ayampi attho vutto bhagavatā, iti me sutanti.
segs.e: This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.
“There is, mendicants, freedom from rebirth, freedom from what has been produced, made, and conditioned.

segs.p: No cetaṁ, bhikkhave, abhavissa ajātaṁ abhūtaṁ akataṁ asaṅkhataṁ, nayidha jātassa bhūtassa katassa saṅkhatassa nissaraṇaṁ paññāyetha.
segs.e: If there were no freedom from rebirth, freedom from what has been produced, made, and conditioned, then you would find no escape here from rebirth, from what has been produced, made, and conditioned.

segs.p: Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, atthi ajātaṁ abhūtaṁ akataṁ asaṅkhataṁ, tasmā jātassa bhūtassa katassa saṅkhatassa nissaraṇaṁ paññāyatī”ti.
segs.e: But since there is freedom from rebirth, freedom from what has been produced, made, and conditioned, an escape is found from rebirth, from what has been produced, made, and conditioned.”
wrapped in old age and death,
whose inception is the leash to food:
that’s not fit to delight in.
The escape from that is peaceful,
beyond the scope of logic, everlasting,
where nothing is reborn or arisen,
the cessation of all painful things,

segs.p: Ayampi attho vutto bhagavatā, iti me sutanti.
segs.e: This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.
“There are, mendicants, these two elements of extinguishment.

segs.p: Saupādisesā ca nibbānadhātu, anupādisesā ca nibbānadhātu.
segs.e: The element of extinguishment with residue, and the element of extinguishment with no residue.
And what is the element of extinguishment with residue?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu arahaṁ hoti khīṇāsavo vusitavā katakaraṇīyo ohitabhāro anuppattasadattho parikkhīṇabhavasaṁyojano sammadaññāvimutto.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant is a perfected one, with defilements ended, who has completed the spiritual journey, done what had to be done, laid down the burden, achieved their heart’s goal, utterly ended the fetter of continued existence, and is rightly freed through enlightenment.

segs.p: Tassa tiṭṭhanteva pañcindriyāni yesaṁ avighātattā manāpāmanāpaṁ paccanubhoti, sukhadukkhaṁ paṭisaṁvedeti.
segs.e: Their five sense faculties still remain. So long as their senses have not gone they continue to experience the agreeable and disagreeable, to feel pleasure and pain.
The ending of greed, hate, and delusion in them
is called the element of extinguishment with residue.
And what is the element of extinguishment with no residue?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu arahaṁ hoti khīṇāsavo vusitavā katakaraṇīyo ohitabhāro anuppattasadattho parikkhīṇabhavasaṁyojano sammadaññāvimutto.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant is a perfected one, with defilements ended, who has completed the spiritual journey, done what had to be done, laid down the burden, achieved their heart’s goal, utterly ended the fetter of continued existence, and is rightly freed through enlightenment.

segs.p: Tassa idheva, bhikkhave, sabbavedayitāni anabhinanditāni sīti bhavissanti.
segs.e: For them, everything that’s felt, being no longer relished, will become cool right here.
This is called the element of extinguishment with no residue.
These are the two elements of extinguishment.”
“These two elements of extinguishment <j>have been revealed
by the Clear-eyed One, <j>the unattached, the unaffected.
One element pertains to this life—
that with residue <j>though the leash to existence has ended;
and that with no residue, <j>which pertains to what follows this life,
where all states of existence cease.
Those who have fully understood <j>the unconditioned state—
their minds freed, the leash to existence ended—
attained to the heart of the Dhamma, <j>they delight in ending,
the unaffected ones have given up <j>all states of existence.”

segs.e: A mendicant who enjoys retreat can expect one of two results:

segs.p: “Dvīhi, bhikkhave, diṭṭhigatehi pariyuṭṭhitā devamanussā olīyanti eke, atidhāvanti eke; cakkhumanto ca passanti.
segs.e: “Overcome by two misconceptions, mendicants, some gods and humans get stuck, some overreach, while those with vision see.
And how do some get stuck?

segs.p: Bhavārāmā, bhikkhave, devamanussā bhavaratā bhavasammuditā tesaṁ bhavanirodhāya dhamme desiyamāne cittaṁ na pakkhandati na pasīdati na santiṭṭhati nādhimuccati.
segs.e: Gods and humans like clinging, they love it and enjoy it. When the Dhamma is being taught to them for the cessation of existence, their minds do not leap forth, gain confidence, settle down, and become decided.
That is how some get stuck.

segs.p: Bhaveneva kho paneke aṭṭīyamānā harāyamānā jigucchamānā vibhavaṁ abhinandanti—
segs.e: Some, becoming horrified, repelled, and disgusted with existence, delight in nonexistence:

segs.p: yato kira, bho, ayaṁ attā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā ucchijjati vinassati na hoti paraṁ maraṇā;
segs.e: ‘When this self is annihilated and destroyed when the body breaks up, and doesn’t exist after death:

segs.p: etaṁ santaṁ etaṁ paṇītaṁ etaṁ yāthāvanti.
segs.e: that is peaceful, that is sublime, that is how it is.’
And how do those with vision see?
It’s when a mendicant sees what has come to be as having come to be.

segs.p: bhūtaṁ bhūtato disvā bhūtassa nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipanno hoti.
segs.e: Seeing this, they are practicing for disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding what has come to be.
That is how those with vision see.”
“Those who see what has come to be <j>as having come to be,
and see the transcendence of what has come to be,
are freed in accord with the truth,
with the ending of craving for continued existence.
They completely understand what has come to be,
rid of craving for rebirth in this or that state.
When what has come to be ceases to be,
a mendicant does not come back to future lives.”

segs.p: ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, ‘abaddho mārassa omukkassa mārapāso na yathākāmakaraṇīyo pāpimato’”ti.

segs.e: is said to have not crossed over the ocean with its waves and whirlpools, its saltwater crocodiles and monsters.

segs.e: “Mendicants, I’ve seen beings who engaged in misconduct by body, speech, and mind, who denounced the noble ones, who had wrong views and acted accordingly.

segs.p: Te kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapannā.

segs.p: Taṁ kho panāhaṁ, bhikkhave, nāññassa samaṇassa vā brāhmaṇassa vā sutvā vadāmi.
segs.e: Now, I don’t say this because I’ve heard it from some other ascetic or brahmin.

segs.p: Diṭṭhā mayā, bhikkhave, sattā kāyaduccaritena samannāgatā vacīduccaritena samannāgatā manoduccaritena samannāgatā ariyānaṁ upavādakā micchādiṭṭhikā micchādiṭṭhikammasamādānā.

segs.e: I only say it because I’ve known, seen, and realized it for myself.”

“Mendicants, these three individuals are found in the world.
One like a rainless cloud, one who rains locally, one who rains all over.

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo sabbesaññeva na dātā hoti, samaṇabrāhmaṇakapaṇaddhikavanibbakayācakānaṁ annaṁ pānaṁ vatthaṁ yānaṁ mālāgandhavilepanaṁ seyyāvasathapadīpeyyaṁ.
segs.e: It’s when an individual doesn’t give to anyone at all—whether ascetics and brahmins, paupers, vagrants, supplicants, or beggars—such things as food, drink, clothing, vehicles; garlands, fragrance, and makeup; and bed, house, and lighting.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo avuṭṭhikasamo hoti.
segs.e: That’s how an individual is like a rainless cloud.
And how does an individual rain locally?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo ekaccānaṁ dātā hoti, ekaccānaṁ na dātā hoti samaṇabrāhmaṇakapaṇaddhikavanibbakayācakānaṁ annaṁ pānaṁ vatthaṁ yānaṁ mālāgandhavilepanaṁ seyyāvasathapadīpeyyaṁ.
segs.e: It’s when an individual gives to some but not to others—whether ascetics and brahmins, paupers, vagrants, supplicants, or beggars—such things as food, drink, clothing, vehicles; garlands, fragrance, and makeup; and bed, house, and lighting.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo padesavassī hoti.
segs.e: That’s how an individual rains locally.
And how does an individual rain all over?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo sabbesaṁva deti, samaṇabrāhmaṇakapaṇaddhikavanibbakayācakānaṁ annaṁ pānaṁ vatthaṁ yānaṁ mālāgandhavilepanaṁ seyyāvasathapadīpeyyaṁ.
segs.e: It’s when an individual gives to everyone—whether ascetics and brahmins, paupers, vagrants, supplicants, or beggars—such things as food, drink, clothing, vehicles; garlands, fragrance, and makeup; and bed, house, and lighting.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo sabbatthābhivassī hoti.
segs.e: That’s how an individual rains all over.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmin”ti.
segs.e: These are the three individuals found in the world.”

segs.p: “Tayome, bhikkhave, devesu devasaddā niccharanti samayā samayaṁ upādāya.
segs.e: “Mendicants, these three cries are uttered among the gods on occasion.

segs.p: Yasmiṁ, bhikkhave, samaye ariyasāvako kesamassuṁ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajjāya ceteti, tasmiṁ samaye devesu devasaddo niccharati:
segs.e: When a noble disciple shaves off their hair and beard, dresses in ocher robes, and goes forth from the lay life to homelessness, the gods cry out:
‘This noble disciple intends to join battle with Māra!’

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, paṭhamo devesu devasaddo niccharati samayā samayaṁ upādāya.
segs.e: This is the first occasion a cry is uttered among the gods.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, yasmiṁ samaye ariyasāvako sattannaṁ bodhipakkhiyānaṁ dhammānaṁ bhāvanānuyogamanuyutto viharati, tasmiṁ samaye devesu devasaddo niccharati:
segs.e: Furthermore, when a noble disciple meditates pursuing the development of the seven qualities on the side of awakening, the gods cry out:
‘This noble disciple is joining battle with Māra!’

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, dutiyo devesu devasaddo niccharati samayā samayaṁ upādāya.
segs.e: This is the second occasion a cry is uttered among the gods.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, yasmiṁ samaye ariyasāvako āsavānaṁ khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati, tasmiṁ samaye devesu devasaddo niccharati:
segs.e: Furthermore, when a noble disciple realizes the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements, the gods cry out:

segs.p: ‘eso ariyasāvako vijitasaṅgāmo tameva saṅgāmasīsaṁ abhivijiya ajjhāvasatī’ti.
segs.e: ‘This noble disciple has won victory in battle, establishing himself as foremost in battle!’

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, tatiyo devesu devasaddo niccharati samayā samayaṁ upādāya.
segs.e: This is the third occasion a cry is uttered among the gods.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo devesu devasaddā niccharanti samayā samayaṁ upādāyā”ti.
segs.e: These are the three cries that are uttered among the gods on occasion.”

segs.p: “Yadā, bhikkhave, devo devakāyā cavanadhammo hoti, pañcassa pubbanimittāni pātubhavanti—
segs.e: “Mendicants, when a god is due to pass away from the realm of the gods, five harbingers appear.

segs.p: mālā milāyanti, vatthāni kilissanti, kacchehi sedā muccanti, kāye dubbaṇṇiyaṁ okkamati, sake devo devāsane nābhiramatīti.
segs.e: Their flower-garlands wither; their clothes become soiled; they sweat from the armpits; their physical appearance deteriorates; and they no longer delight in their heavenly throne.

segs.p: Tamenaṁ, bhikkhave, devā ‘cavanadhammo ayaṁ devaputto’ti iti viditvā tīhi vācāhi anumodenti:
segs.e: When the other gods know that that godling is due to pass away, they wish them well in three ways:
‘Sir, may you go from here to a good place!
When you have gone to a good place, may you be blessed with good fortune!
When you have been blessed with good fortune, may you become well grounded!’”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, aññataro bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he said this, one of the mendicants said to the Buddha,
“Sir, what do the gods reckon to be going to a good place?
What do they reckon to be blessed with good fortune?
What do they reckon to become well grounded?”
“It is human existence, mendicant, that the gods reckon to be going to a good place.

segs.p: Yaṁ manussabhūto samāno tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye saddhaṁ paṭilabhati;
segs.e: When a human being gains faith in the teaching and training proclaimed by the Realized One,
that is what the gods reckon to be blessed with good fortune.

segs.p: Sā kho panassa saddhā niviṭṭhā hoti mūlajātā patiṭṭhitā daḷhā asaṁhāriyā samaṇena vā brāhmaṇena vā devena vā mārena vā brahmunā vā kenaci vā lokasmiṁ;
segs.e: When that faith in the Realized One is settled, rooted, and planted deep; when it’s strong and can’t be shifted by any ascetic or brahmin or god or Māra or divinity or by anyone in the world,
that is what the gods reckon to become well grounded.”

For the Welfare of the People
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.

segs.p: “Tayome puggalā loke uppajjamānā uppajjanti bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṁ.
segs.e: “These three individuals, mendicants, arise in the world for the welfare and happiness of the people, out of sympathy for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, tathāgato loke uppajjati arahaṁ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṁ buddho bhagavā.
segs.e: It’s when a Realized One arises in the world, perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.

segs.p: So dhammaṁ deseti ādikalyāṇaṁ majjhekalyāṇaṁ pariyosānakalyāṇaṁ sātthaṁ sabyañjanaṁ, kevalaparipuṇṇaṁ parisuddhaṁ brahmacariyaṁ pakāseti.
segs.e: He teaches Dhamma that’s good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased. And he reveals a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, paṭhamo puggalo loke uppajjamāno uppajjati bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṁ.
segs.e: This is the first individual who arises in the world for the welfare and happiness of the people, out of sympathy for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, tasseva satthu sāvako arahaṁ hoti khīṇāsavo vusitavā katakaraṇīyo ohitabhāro anuppattasadattho parikkhīṇabhavasaṁyojano sammadaññāvimutto.
segs.e: Furthermore, it’s when a mendicant is a perfected one, with defilements ended, who has completed the spiritual journey, done what had to be done, laid down the burden, achieved their heart’s goal, utterly ended the fetter of continued existence, and is rightly freed through enlightenment.

segs.p: So dhammaṁ deseti ādikalyāṇaṁ majjhekalyāṇaṁ pariyosānakalyāṇaṁ sātthaṁ sabyañjanaṁ, kevalaparipuṇṇaṁ parisuddhaṁ brahmacariyaṁ pakāseti.
segs.e: They teach Dhamma that’s good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased. And they reveal a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, dutiyo puggalo loke uppajjamāno uppajjati bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṁ.
segs.e: This is the second individual who arises in the world for the welfare and happiness of the people, out of sympathy for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, tasseva satthu sāvako sekho hoti pāṭipado bahussuto sīlavatūpapanno.
segs.e: Furthermore, it’s when a disciple of that Teacher is a trainee, a learned practitioner with precepts and observances intact.

segs.p: Sopi dhammaṁ deseti ādikalyāṇaṁ majjhekalyāṇaṁ pariyosānakalyāṇaṁ sātthaṁ sabyañjanaṁ, kevalaparipuṇṇaṁ parisuddhaṁ brahmacariyaṁ pakāseti.
segs.e: They teach Dhamma that’s good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased. And they reveal a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, tatiyo puggalo loke uppajjamāno uppajjati bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṁ.
segs.e: This is the third individual who arises in the world for the welfare and happiness of the people, out of sympathy for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo puggalā loke uppajjamānā uppajjanti bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānan”ti.
segs.e: These are the three individuals who arise in the world for the welfare and happiness of the people, out of sympathy for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.”
“The Teacher is the first, the great seer,
following whom is the evolved disciple,
and then a trainee, a practitioner,
learned, with precepts and observances intact.
These three are first among gods and humans,
They fling open the door to freedom from death,
Following the path so well taught
those who are diligent in the Holy One’s teaching
make an end of suffering in this very life.”

segs.p: Ayampi attho vutto bhagavatā, iti me sutanti.

“Mendicants, meditate observing the ugliness of the body.

segs.p: ānāpānassati ca vo ajjhattaṁ parimukhaṁ sūpaṭṭhitā hotu;
segs.e: Let mindfulness of breathing be well-established internally on the present.
Meditate observing the impermanence of all conditions.

segs.p: Asubhānupassīnaṁ, bhikkhave, kāyasmiṁ viharataṁ yo subhāya dhātuyā rāgānusayo so pahīyati.
segs.e: As you meditate observing the ugliness of the body, you will give up desire for the body.

segs.p: Ānāpānassatiyā ajjhattaṁ parimukhaṁ sūpaṭṭhititāya ye bāhirā vitakkāsayā vighātapakkhikā, te na honti.
segs.e: When mindfulness of breathing is well-established internally on the present, there will be no distressing external thoughts or wishes.

segs.p: Sabbasaṅkhāresu aniccānupassīnaṁ viharataṁ yā avijjā sā pahīyati, yā vijjā sā uppajjatī”ti.
segs.e: When you meditate observing the impermanence of all conditions, ignorance is given up and knowledge arises.”

Practicing In Line With the Teaching
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.
“Regarding a mendicant practicing in line with the teaching, it is in line with the teaching to declare that

segs.p: dhammānudhammapaṭipannoyanti bhāsamāno dhammaññeva bhāsati no adhammaṁ, vitakkayamāno vā dhammavitakkaññeva vitakketi no adhammavitakkaṁ, tadubhayaṁ vā pana abhinivejjetvā upekkhako viharati sato sampajāno”ti.
segs.e: this is what it means to practice in line with the teaching. When speaking, they speak on the teaching, not against it. When thinking, they think on the teaching, not against it. And rejecting both, they meditate staying equanimous, mindful and aware.”
“Delighting in the teaching, enjoying the teaching,
a mendicant who recollects the teaching
doesn’t fall away from the true teaching.

segs.p: “Tayome, bhikkhave, akusalavitakkā andhakaraṇā acakkhukaraṇā aññāṇakaraṇā paññānirodhikā vighātapakkhikā anibbānasaṁvattanikā.
segs.e: “Mendicants, these three unskillful thoughts are destroyers of sight, vision, and knowledge. They block wisdom, they’re on the side of distress, and they don’t lead to extinguishment.

segs.p: Kāmavitakko, bhikkhave, andhakaraṇo acakkhukaraṇo aññāṇakaraṇo paññānirodhiko vighātapakkhiko anibbānasaṁvattaniko.
Byāpādavitakko, bhikkhave, andhakaraṇo acakkhukaraṇo aññāṇakaraṇo paññānirodhiko vighātapakkhiko anibbānasaṁvattaniko.
Vihiṁsāvitakko, bhikkhave, andhakaraṇo acakkhukaraṇo aññāṇakaraṇo paññānirodhiko vighātapakkhiko anibbānasaṁvattaniko.
Ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo akusalavitakkā andhakaraṇā acakkhukaraṇā aññāṇakaraṇā paññānirodhikā vighātapakkhikā anibbānasaṁvattanikā.
segs.e: These are the three unskillful thoughts that are destroyers of sight, vision, and knowledge. They block wisdom, they’re on the side of distress, and they don’t lead to extinguishment.

segs.p: Tayome, bhikkhave, kusalavitakkā anandhakaraṇā cakkhukaraṇā ñāṇakaraṇā paññāvuddhikā avighātapakkhikā nibbānasaṁvattanikā.
segs.e: These three skillful thoughts are creators of sight, vision, and knowledge. They grow wisdom, they’re on the side of solace, and they lead to extinguishment.

segs.p: Nekkhammavitakko, bhikkhave, anandhakaraṇo cakkhukaraṇo ñāṇakaraṇo paññāvuddhiko avighātapakkhiko nibbānasaṁvattaniko.
Abyāpādavitakko, bhikkhave, anandhakaraṇo cakkhukaraṇo ñāṇakaraṇo paññāvuddhiko avighātapakkhiko nibbānasaṁvattaniko.
Avihiṁsāvitakko, bhikkhave, anandhakaraṇo cakkhukaraṇo ñāṇakaraṇo paññāvuddhiko avighātapakkhiko nibbānasaṁvattaniko.
Ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo kusalavitakkā anandhakaraṇā cakkhukaraṇā ñāṇakaraṇā paññāvuddhikā avighātapakkhikā nibbānasaṁvattanikā”ti.
segs.e: These are the three skillful thoughts that are creators of sight, vision, and knowledge. They grow wisdom, they’re on the side of solace, and they lead to extinguishment.”

segs.p: “Tayome, bhikkhave, antarāmalā antarāamittā antarāsapattā antarāvadhakā antarāpaccatthikā.
segs.e: “Mendicants, there are these three inner stains, inner foes, inner enemies, inner killers, and inner adversaries.

segs.p: Lobho, bhikkhave, antarāmalo antarāamitto antarāsapatto antarāvadhako antarāpaccatthiko.
Doso, bhikkhave, antarāmalo antarāamitto antarāsapatto antarāvadhako antarāpaccatthiko.
Moho, bhikkhave, antarāmalo antarāamitto antarāsapatto antarāvadhako antarāpaccatthiko.
Ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo antarāmalā antarāamittā antarāsapattā antarāvadhakā antarāpaccatthikā”ti.
segs.e: These three are inner stains, inner foes, inner enemies, inner killers, and inner adversaries.”

segs.p: “Tīhi, bhikkhave, asaddhammehi abhibhūto pariyādinnacitto devadatto āpāyiko nerayiko kappaṭṭho atekiccho.
segs.e: “Mendicants, overcome and overwhelmed by three things that oppose the true teaching, Devadatta is going to a place of loss, to hell, there to remain for an eon, irredeemable.

segs.p: Pāpicchatāya, bhikkhave, abhibhūto pariyādinnacitto devadatto āpāyiko nerayiko kappaṭṭho atekiccho.
Pāpamittatāya, bhikkhave, abhibhūto pariyādinnacitto devadatto āpāyiko nerayiko kappaṭṭho atekiccho.

segs.e: When there is still more to be done, stopping half-way after achieving some trifling distinction.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhi asaddhammehi abhibhūto pariyādinnacitto devadatto āpāyiko nerayiko kappaṭṭho atekiccho”ti.
segs.e: Overcome and overwhelmed by these three things that oppose the true teaching, Devadatta is going to a place of loss, to hell, there to remain for an eon, irredeemable.”

A mendicant who walks the path

segs.p: Ayampi attho vutto bhagavatā, iti me sutanti.

“Mendicants, these three kinds of confidence are the best.

segs.p: Yāvatā, bhikkhave, sattā apadā vā dvipadā vā catuppadā vā bahuppadā vā rūpino vā arūpino vā saññino vā asaññino vā nevasaññināsaññino vā, tathāgato tesaṁ aggamakkhāyati arahaṁ sammāsambuddho.
segs.e: Mendicants, the Realized One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha, is said to be the best of all sentient beings—be they footless, with two feet, four feet, or many feet; with form or formless; with perception or without perception or with neither perception nor non-perception.

segs.p: Ye, bhikkhave, buddhe pasannā, agge te pasannā.
segs.e: Those who have confidence in the Buddha have confidence in the best.

segs.p: Agge kho pana pasannānaṁ aggo vipāko hoti.
segs.e: Having confidence in the best, the result is the best.

segs.p: Yāvatā, bhikkhave, dhammā saṅkhatā vā asaṅkhatā vā, virāgo tesaṁ aggamakkhāyati, yadidaṁ madanimmadano pipāsavinayo ālayasamugghāto vaṭṭupacchedo taṇhakkhayo virāgo nirodho nibbānaṁ.
segs.e: Fading away is said to be the best of all things whether conditioned or unconditioned. That is, the quelling of vanity, the removing of thirst, the uprooting of clinging, the breaking of the round, the ending of craving, fading away, cessation, extinguishment.

segs.p: Ye, bhikkhave, virāge dhamme pasannā, agge te pasannā.
segs.e: Those who have confidence in the teaching of fading away have confidence in the best.

segs.p: Agge kho pana pasannānaṁ aggo vipāko hoti.
segs.e: Having confidence in the best, the result is the best.

segs.p: Yāvatā, bhikkhave, saṅghā vā gaṇā vā, tathāgatasāvakasaṅgho tesaṁ aggamakkhāyati, yadidaṁ cattāri purisayugāni aṭṭha purisapuggalā esa bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho āhuneyyo pāhuneyyo dakkhiṇeyyo añjalikaraṇīyo anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassa.
segs.e: The Saṅgha of the Realized One’s disciples is said to be the best of all communities and groups. It consists of the four pairs, the eight individual persons. This is the Saṅgha of the Buddha’s disciples that is worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of greeting with cupped palms, and is the supreme field of merit for the world.

segs.p: Ye, bhikkhave, saṅghe pasannā, agge te pasannā.
segs.e: Those who have confidence in the Saṅgha have confidence in the best.

segs.p: Agge kho pana pasannānaṁ aggo vipāko hoti.
segs.e: Having confidence in the best, the result is the best.
These are the three best kinds of confidence.”
“For those who, knowing the best teaching,
base their confidence on the best—
confident in the best Awakened One,
supremely worthy of a religious donation;
the bliss of fading and stilling;
An intelligent person gives to the best,
When they become a god or human,
they rejoice at reaching the best.”

segs.p: Ayampi attho vutto bhagavatā, iti me sutanti.
segs.e: This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.
“This is the last of lifestyles, mendicants, namely relying on alms.
The world curses you: ‘You beggar, walking bowl in hand!’

segs.p: Tañca kho etaṁ, bhikkhave, kulaputtā upenti atthavasikā, atthavasaṁ paṭicca;
segs.e: Yet earnest gentlemen take it up for a good reason.

segs.p: neva rājābhinītā, na corābhinītā, na iṇaṭṭā, na bhayaṭṭā, na ājīvikāpakatā.
segs.e: Not to escape a summons by a king or a summons for a bandit, or because you were in debt or in fear, or in order to make a living.

segs.p: Api ca kho ‘otiṇṇamhā jātiyā jarāya maraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi dukkhotiṇṇā dukkhaparetā,
segs.e: Rather, because they think: ‘I’m swamped by rebirth, old age, and death; by sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress. I’m swamped by suffering, mired in suffering.

segs.p: appeva nāma imassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa antakiriyā paññāyethā’ti.
segs.e: Hopefully I can make an end to this entire mass of suffering.’
That’s how this gentleman has gone forth.

segs.p: So ca hoti abhijjhālu kāmesu tibbasārāgo, byāpannacitto paduṭṭhamanasaṅkappo, muṭṭhassati asampajāno asamāhito vibbhantacitto pākatindriyo.
segs.e: Yet they covet sensual pleasures; they’re infatuated, full of ill will and malicious intent. They are unmindful, lacking situational awareness and immersion, with straying minds and undisciplined faculties.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, chavālātaṁ ubhatopadittaṁ majjhe gūthagataṁ neva gāme kaṭṭhatthaṁ pharati na araññe;
segs.e: Suppose there was a firebrand for lighting a funeral pyre, burning at both ends, and smeared with dung in the middle. It couldn’t be used as timber either in the village or the wilderness.

segs.p: tathūpamāhaṁ, bhikkhave, imaṁ puggalaṁ vadāmi gihibhogā parihīno sāmaññatthañca na paripūretī”ti.
segs.e: I say that individual is just like this. They’ve missed out on the pleasures of the lay life, and haven’t fulfilled the goal of the ascetic life.”
“They’ve left behind the pleasures of the lay life,
and miss out on the goal of the ascetic life.
Ruining it, they throw it away,
and perish like a funeral firebrand.
Many who wear a scrap of ocher cloth
Being wicked, they are reborn in hell
It’d be better for the immoral and unrestrained
than to eat the nation’s alms.”

segs.p: Ayampi attho vutto bhagavatā, iti me sutanti.
segs.e: This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.

segs.p: “Saṅghāṭikaṇṇe cepi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu gahetvā piṭṭhito piṭṭhito anubandho assa pāde pādaṁ nikkhipanto,
segs.e: “Mendicants, suppose a mendicant were to hold the corner of my cloak and follow behind me step by step.

segs.p: so ca hoti abhijjhālu kāmesu tibbasārāgo byāpannacitto paduṭṭhamanasaṅkappo muṭṭhassati asampajāno asamāhito vibbhantacitto pākatindriyo;
segs.e: Yet they covet sensual pleasures; they’re infatuated, full of ill will and malicious intent. They are unmindful, lacking situational awareness and immersion, with straying minds and undisciplined faculties.

segs.p: atha kho so ārakāva mayhaṁ, ahañca tassa.
segs.e: Then they are far from me, and I from them.

segs.p: Dhammañhi so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na passati.
segs.e: Because that mendicant does not see the teaching.
Not seeing the teaching, they do not see me.

segs.p: Yojanasate cepi so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu vihareyya.

segs.e: Yet they do not covet sensual pleasures; they’re not infatuated, or full of ill will and malicious intent. They have established mindfulness, situational awareness and immersion, with unified mind and restrained faculties.

segs.p: “Tathā tathā, bhikkhave, bhikkhu upaparikkheyya yathā yathāssa upaparikkhato bahiddhā cassa viññāṇaṁ avikkhittaṁ avisaṭaṁ ajjhattaṁ asaṇṭhitaṁ anupādāya na paritasseyya.
segs.e: “A mendicant should examine in whatever way such that, while examining, consciousness would neither be scattered nor diffused externally, nor stuck internally, and they would not be anxious because of grasping.

segs.p: Bahiddhā, bhikkhave, viññāṇe avikkhitte avisaṭe sati ajjhattaṁ asaṇṭhite anupādāya aparitassato āyatiṁ jātijarāmaraṇadukkhasamudayasambhavo na hotī”ti.
segs.e: When consciousness is neither scattered nor diffused externally, nor stuck internally, and they are not anxious because of grasping, there is no coming to be of the origin of suffering—of rebirth, old age, and death in the future.”
“For one who has given up seven chains,
a mendicant who has cut the cord,
there’ll be no more future lives for them.”

segs.p: Ayampi attho vutto bhagavatā, iti me sutanti.
segs.e: This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.

segs.p: “Kāmayogayutto, bhikkhave, bhavayogayutto āgāmī hoti āgantā itthattaṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, one yoked to both sensual pleasures and rebirth is a returner, who comes back to this place.

segs.p: Kāmayogavisaṁyutto, bhikkhave, bhavayogayutto anāgāmī hoti anāgantā itthattaṁ.
segs.e: One unyoked from sensual pleasures but still yoked to rebirth is a non-returner, who comes not back to this place.

segs.p: Kāmayogavisaṁyutto, bhikkhave, bhavayogavisaṁyutto arahā hoti, khīṇāsavo”ti.
segs.e: One unyoked from both sensual pleasures and rebirth is a perfected one, who has ended defilements.”

Those who have cut off doubt,

segs.p: Ayampi attho vutto bhagavatā, iti me sutanti.

segs.p: “Kalyāṇasīlo, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kalyāṇadhammo kalyāṇapañño imasmiṁ dhammavinaye ‘kevalī vusitavā uttamapuriso’ti vuccati—
segs.e: “Mendicants, in this teaching and training a mendicant of good morals, good practice, and good wisdom is called consummate, accomplished, a supreme person.
And how does a mendicant have good morals?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sīlavā hoti, pātimokkhasaṁvarasaṁvuto viharati, ācāragocarasampanno aṇumattesu vajjesu bhayadassāvī, samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesu.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant is ethical, restrained in the monastic code, conducting themselves well and resorting for alms in suitable places. Seeing danger in the slightest fault, they keep the rules they’ve undertaken.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kalyāṇasīlo hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a mendicant has good morals.
Such is one of good morality.
And how does one have good practice?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sattannaṁ bodhipakkhiyānaṁ dhammānaṁ bhāvanānuyogamanuyutto viharati.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant meditates pursuing the development of the seven qualities on the side of awakening.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kalyāṇadhammo hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a mendicant has good practice.
Such is one of good morality and good practice.
And how does one have good wisdom?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu āsavānaṁ khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant realizes the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kalyāṇapañño hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a mendicant has good wisdom;

segs.p: Iti kalyāṇasīlo kalyāṇadhammo kalyāṇapañño imasmiṁ dhammavinaye ‘kevalī vusitavā uttamapuriso’ti vuccatī”ti.
segs.e: Such is one of good morals, good practice, and good wisdom, who in this teaching and training is called consummate, accomplished, a supreme person.”
is said to be one of good morals,

One accomplished in these three things,

segs.p: Ayampi attho vutto bhagavatā, iti me sutanti.
segs.e: This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.

A gift of things of the flesh and a gift of the teaching.

segs.p: Etadaggaṁ, bhikkhave, imesaṁ dvinnaṁ dānānaṁ yadidaṁ dhammadānaṁ.
segs.e: The better of these two gifts is the gift of the teaching.
There are these two kinds of sharing.
Sharing things of the flesh and sharing the teaching.

segs.p: Etadaggaṁ, bhikkhave, imesaṁ dvinnaṁ saṁvibhāgānaṁ yadidaṁ dhammasaṁvibhāgo.
segs.e: The better of these two kinds of sharing is sharing the teaching.
There are these two kinds of support.
Support in things of the flesh and support in the teaching.

“It is said to be the supreme, ultimate gift,
and the sharing praised by the Buddha;
what wise and sensible person, <j>confident in the best of fields,

segs.p: “Dhammenāhaṁ, bhikkhave, tevijjaṁ brāhmaṇaṁ paññāpemi, nāññaṁ lapitalāpanamattena.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I define a brahmin in terms of the teaching as one who is master of the three knowledges, not the other who merely repeats what they are told.

segs.p: Kathañcāhaṁ, bhikkhave, dhammena tevijjaṁ brāhmaṇaṁ paññāpemi, nāññaṁ lapitalāpanamattena?

Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu anekavihitaṁ pubbenivāsaṁ anussarati, seyyathidaṁ—ekampi jātiṁ dvepi jātiyo tissopi jātiyo catassopi jātiyo pañcapi jātiyo dasapi jātiyo vīsampi jātiyo tiṁsampi jātiyo cattālīsampi jātiyo paññāsampi jātiyo jātisatampi jātisahassampi jātisatasahassampi anekepi saṁvaṭṭakappe anekepi vivaṭṭakappe anekepi saṁvaṭṭavivaṭṭakappe: ‘amutrāsiṁ evaṁnāmo evaṅgotto evaṁvaṇṇo evamāhāro evaṁsukhadukkhappaṭisaṁvedī evamāyupariyanto. So tato cuto amutra udapādiṁ. Tatrāpāsiṁ evaṁnāmo evaṅgotto evaṁvaṇṇo evamāhāro evaṁsukhadukkhappaṭisaṁvedī evamāyupariyanto. So tato cuto idhūpapanno’ti. Iti sākāraṁ sauddesaṁ anekavihitaṁ pubbenivāsaṁ anussarati.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant recollects many kinds of past lives. That is: one, two, three, four, five, ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, a hundred, a thousand, a hundred thousand rebirths; many eons of the world contracting, many eons of the world expanding, many eons of the world contracting and expanding. They remember: ‘There, I was named this, my clan was that, I looked like this, and that was my food. This was how I felt pleasure and pain, and that was how my life ended. When I passed away from that place I was reborn somewhere else. There, too, I was named this, my clan was that, I looked like this, and that was my food. This was how I felt pleasure and pain, and that was how my life ended. When I passed away from that place I was reborn here.’ And so they recollect their many kinds of past lives, with features and details.

segs.p: Ayamassa paṭhamā vijjā adhigatā hoti, avijjā vihatā, vijjā uppannā, tamo vihato, āloko uppanno, yathā taṁ appamattassa ātāpino pahitattassa viharato.
segs.e: This is the first knowledge they achieved. Ignorance was banished and knowledge arose; darkness was banished and light arose, as happens for a meditator who is diligent, keen, and resolute.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena satte passati cavamāne upapajjamāne hīne paṇīte suvaṇṇe dubbaṇṇe, sugate duggate yathākammūpage satte pajānāti: ‘ime vata bhonto sattā kāyaduccaritena samannāgatā vacīduccaritena samannāgatā manoduccaritena samannāgatā ariyānaṁ upavādakā micchādiṭṭhikā micchādiṭṭhikammasamādānā. Te kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapannā. Ime vā pana bhonto sattā kāyasucaritena samannāgatā vacīsucaritena samannāgatā manosucaritena samannāgatā ariyānaṁ anupavādakā sammādiṭṭhikā sammādiṭṭhikammasamādānā. Te kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapannā’ti. Iti dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena satte passati cavamāne upapajjamāne hīne paṇīte suvaṇṇe dubbaṇṇe, sugate duggate yathākammūpage satte pajānāti.
segs.e: Furthermore, with clairvoyance that is purified and superhuman, a mendicant sees sentient beings passing away and being reborn—inferior and superior, beautiful and ugly, in a good place or a bad place. They understand how sentient beings pass on according to their deeds: ‘These dear beings did bad things by way of body, speech, and mind. They denounced the noble ones; they had wrong view; and they chose to act out of that wrong view. When their body broke up, after death, they were reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell. These dear beings, however, did good things by way of body, speech, and mind. They never denounced the noble ones; they had right view; and they chose to act out of that right view. When their body broke up, after death, they were reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.’ And so, with clairvoyance that is purified and superhuman, they see sentient beings passing away and being reborn—inferior and superior, beautiful and ugly, in a good place or a bad place. They understand how sentient beings pass on according to their deeds.

segs.p: Ayamassa dutiyā vijjā adhigatā hoti, avijjā vihatā, vijjā uppannā, tamo vihato, āloko uppanno, yathā taṁ appamattassa ātāpino pahitattassa viharato.
segs.e: This is the second knowledge they achieved. Ignorance was banished and knowledge arose; darkness was banished and light arose, as happens for a meditator who is diligent, keen, and resolute.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu āsavānaṁ khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant realizes the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.

segs.p: Ayamassa tatiyā vijjā adhigatā hoti, avijjā vihatā, vijjā uppannā, tamo vihato, āloko uppanno, yathā taṁ appamattassa ātāpino pahitattassa viharato.
segs.e: This is the third knowledge which they achieved. Ignorance was banished and knowledge arose; darkness was banished and light arose, as happens for a meditator who is diligent, keen, and resolute.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho ahaṁ, bhikkhave, dhammena tevijjaṁ brāhmaṇaṁ paññāpemi, nāññaṁ lapitalāpanamattenā”ti.
segs.e: That’s how I define a brahmin in terms of the teaching as one who is master of the three knowledges, not the other who merely repeats what they are told.”
sees heaven and places of loss,

a brahmin is a master of the three knowledges.

segs.p: “Ahamasmi, bhikkhave, brāhmaṇo yācayogo sadā payatapāṇi antimadehadharo anuttaro bhisakko sallakatto.
segs.e: “I, mendicants, am a brahmin, committed to charity, always open-handed, bearing my final body, a healer, a surgeon.

segs.p: Tassa me tumhe puttā orasā mukhato jātā dhammajā dhammanimmitā dhammadāyādā, no āmisadāyādā.
segs.e: You are my bosom sons, born from my mouth, born of the teaching, created by the teaching, heirs in the teaching, not in things of the flesh.
A gift of things of the flesh and a gift of the teaching.

segs.p: Etadaggaṁ, bhikkhave, imesaṁ dvinnaṁ dānānaṁ yadidaṁ dhammadānaṁ.
segs.e: The better of these two gifts is the gift of the teaching.
There are these two kinds of sharing.
Sharing things of the flesh and sharing the teaching.

segs.p: Etadaggaṁ, bhikkhave, imesaṁ dvinnaṁ saṁvibhāgānaṁ yadidaṁ dhammasaṁvibhāgo.
segs.e: The better of these two kinds of sharing is sharing the teaching.
There are these two kinds of support.
Support in things of the flesh and support in the teaching.

segs.p: Etadaggaṁ, bhikkhave, imesaṁ dvinnaṁ anuggahānaṁ yadidaṁ dhammānuggaho.
segs.e: The better of these two kinds of support is support in the teaching.
An offering of things of the flesh and an offering of the teaching.

segs.p: Etadaggaṁ, bhikkhave, imesaṁ dvinnaṁ yāgānaṁ yadidaṁ dhammayāgo”ti.
segs.e: The better of these two offerings is an offering of the teaching.”

Sentient beings revere him, <j>first among gods and humans,

segs.p: “Cattārimāni, bhikkhave, appāni ceva sulabhāni ca, tāni ca anavajjāni.
segs.e: “Mendicants, these four trifles are easy to find and are blameless.

segs.p: Paṁsukūlaṁ, bhikkhave, cīvarānaṁ appañca sulabhañca, tañca anavajjaṁ.
Piṇḍiyālopo, bhikkhave, bhojanānaṁ appañca sulabhañca, tañca anavajjaṁ.
Rukkhamūlaṁ, bhikkhave, senāsanānaṁ appañca sulabhañca, tañca anavajjaṁ.
segs.e: Lodgings at the root of a tree …

segs.p: Pūtimuttaṁ, bhikkhave, bhesajjānaṁ appañca sulabhañca tañca anavajjaṁ.
Imāni kho, bhikkhave, cattāri appāni ceva sulabhāni ca, tāni ca anavajjāni.
segs.e: These four trifles are easy to find and are blameless.

segs.p: Yato kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu appena ca tuṭṭho hoti sulabhena ca anavajjena ca, idamassāhaṁ aññataraṁ sāmaññaṅganti vadāmī”ti.
segs.e: When a mendicant is content with trifles that are easy to find, they have one of the factors of the ascetic life, I say.”

These qualities are said to be

segs.p: “Jānatohaṁ, bhikkhave, passato āsavānaṁ khayaṁ vadāmi, no ajānato no apassato.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I say that the ending of defilements is for one who knows and sees, not for one who does not know or see.

segs.p: Kiñca, bhikkhave, jānato, kiṁ passato āsavānaṁ khayo hoti?
segs.e: For one who knows and sees what?

segs.p: Idaṁ dukkhanti, bhikkhave, jānato passato āsavānaṁ khayo hoti. Ayaṁ dukkhasamudayoti, bhikkhave, jānato passato āsavānaṁ khayo hoti. Ayaṁ dukkhanirodhoti, bhikkhave, jānato passato āsavānaṁ khayo hoti. Ayaṁ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadāti, bhikkhave, jānato passato āsavānaṁ khayo hoti.
segs.e: The ending of defilements is for one who knows and sees suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, jānato evaṁ passato āsavānaṁ khayo hotī”ti.
segs.e: The ending of the defilements is for one who knows and sees this.”

segs.p: “Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā ‘idaṁ dukkhan’ti yathābhūtaṁ nappajānanti; ‘ayaṁ dukkhasamudayo’ti yathābhūtaṁ nappajānanti; ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodho’ti yathābhūtaṁ nappajānanti; ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṁ nappajānanti—
segs.e: “Mendicants, there are ascetics and brahmins who don’t truly understand about suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path.

segs.p: na me te, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā samaṇesu vā samaṇasammatā brāhmaṇesu vā brāhmaṇasammatā, na ca panete āyasmanto sāmaññatthaṁ vā brahmaññatthaṁ vā diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharanti.
segs.e: I don’t deem them as true ascetics and brahmins. Those venerables don’t realize the goal of life as an ascetic or brahmin, and don’t live having realized it with their own insight in this very life.

segs.p: Ye ca kho keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā ‘idaṁ dukkhan’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānanti; ‘ayaṁ dukkhasamudayo’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānanti; ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodho’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānanti; ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānanti—
segs.e: There are ascetics and brahmins who truly understand about suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path.

segs.p: te kho me, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā samaṇesu ceva samaṇasammatā brāhmaṇesu ca brāhmaṇasammatā, te ca panāyasmanto sāmaññatthañca brahmaññatthañca diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharantī”ti.
segs.e: I regard them as true ascetics and brahmins. Those venerables realize the goal of life as an ascetic or brahmin, and live having realized it with their own insight.”

segs.p: “Ye te, bhikkhave, bhikkhū sīlasampannā samādhisampannā paññāsampannā vimuttisampannā vimuttiñāṇadassanasampannā ovādakā viññāpakā sandassakā samādapakā samuttejakā sampahaṁsakā alaṁsamakkhātāro saddhammassa dassanampahaṁ, bhikkhave, tesaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ bahūpakāraṁ vadāmi;
segs.e: “Mendicants, take a mendicant who is accomplished in ethics, immersion, wisdom, freedom, and the knowledge and vision of freedom. They advise and instruct. They educate, encourage, fire up, and inspire, and can rightly explain the true teaching. Even the sight of those mendicants is very helpful, I say.

segs.p: savanampahaṁ, bhikkhave, tesaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ bahūpakāraṁ vadāmi;
upasaṅkamanampahaṁ, bhikkhave, tesaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ bahūpakāraṁ vadāmi;
payirupāsanampahaṁ, bhikkhave, tesaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ bahūpakāraṁ vadāmi;
anussaraṇampahaṁ, bhikkhave, tesaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ bahūpakāraṁ vadāmi;
anupabbajjampahaṁ, bhikkhave, tesaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ bahūpakāraṁ vadāmi.
segs.e: or go forth after them is very helpful, I say.

segs.p: Tathārūpe, bhikkhave, bhikkhū sevato bhajato payirupāsato aparipūropi sīlakkhandho bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchati, aparipūropi samādhikkhandho bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchati, aparipūropi paññākkhandho bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchati, aparipūropi vimuttikkhandho bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchati, aparipūropi vimuttiñāṇadassanakkhandho bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchati.
segs.e: For one who frequents and associates with such mendicants, their incomplete spectrum of ethics is completed. Their incomplete spectrum of immersion … wisdom … freedom … knowledge and vision of freedom is completed.

segs.p: Evarūpā ca te, bhikkhave, bhikkhū satthārotipi vuccanti, satthavāhātipi vuccanti, raṇañjahātipi vuccanti, tamonudātipi vuccanti, ālokakarātipi vuccanti, obhāsakarātipi vuccanti, pajjotakarātipi vuccanti, ukkādhārātipi vuccanti, pabhaṅkarātipi vuccanti, ariyātipi vuccanti, cakkhumantotipi vuccantī”ti.
segs.e: Such mendicants are called ‘teachers’, ‘caravan leaders’, ‘strife-discarders’, ‘dispellers of darkness’, ‘bringers of light’, ‘luminaries’, ‘lamps’, ‘candlebearers’, ‘beacons’, ‘noble ones’, and ‘clear-eyed ones’.”

segs.p: “Cattārome, bhikkhave, taṇhuppādā, yattha bhikkhuno taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati.
segs.e: “Mendicants, there are four things that give rise to craving in a mendicant.

segs.p: Cīvarahetu vā, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati;
piṇḍapātahetu vā, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati;
senāsanahetu vā, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati;
itibhavābhavahetu vā, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati.
segs.e: or rebirth in this or that state.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro taṇhuppādā yattha bhikkhuno taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjatī”ti.
segs.e: These are the four things that give rise to craving in a mendicant.”
