segs.p: “Sabrahmakāni, bhikkhave, tāni kulāni yesaṁ puttānaṁ mātāpitaro ajjhāgāre pūjitā honti.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a family where the children honor their parents in their home is said to live with Divinity.

segs.p: Sapubbadevatāni, bhikkhave, tāni kulāni yesaṁ puttānaṁ mātāpitaro ajjhāgāre pūjitā honti.
segs.e: A family where the children honor their parents in their home is said to live with the elder gods.

segs.p: Sapubbācariyakāni, bhikkhave, tāni kulāni yesaṁ puttānaṁ mātāpitaro ajjhāgāre pūjitā honti.
segs.e: A family where the children honor their parents in their home is said to live with the first tutors.

segs.p: Sāhuneyyakāni, bhikkhave, tāni kulāni yesaṁ puttānaṁ mātāpitaro ajjhāgāre pūjitā honti.
segs.e: A family where the children honor their parents in their home is said to live with those worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods.
‘Divinity’ is a term for your parents.
‘Elder gods’ is a term for your parents.
‘First tutors’ is a term for your parents.
‘Worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods’ is a term for your parents.

segs.p: Bahukārā, bhikkhave, mātāpitaro puttānaṁ āpādakā posakā imassa lokassa dassetāro”ti.
segs.e: Parents are very helpful to their children, they raise them, nurture them, and show them the world.”
They’re worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods <j>from their children,
would revere them and honor them
they’re praised in this life by the astute,

segs.p: “Bahukārā, bhikkhave, brāhmaṇagahapatikā tumhākaṁ ye vo paccupaṭṭhitā cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhārehi.
segs.e: “Mendicants, brahmins and householders are very helpful to you, as they provide you with robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.

segs.p: Tumhepi, bhikkhave, bahukārā brāhmaṇagahapatikānaṁ yaṁ nesaṁ dhammaṁ desetha ādikalyāṇaṁ majjhekalyāṇaṁ pariyosānakalyāṇaṁ sātthaṁ sabyañjanaṁ, kevalaparipuṇṇaṁ parisuddhaṁ brahmacariyaṁ pakāsetha.
segs.e: And you are very helpful to brahmins and householders, as you teach them the Dhamma that’s good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased. And you reveal a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure.

segs.p: Evamidaṁ, bhikkhave, aññamaññaṁ nissāya brahmacariyaṁ vussati oghassa nittharaṇatthāya sammā dukkhassa antakiriyāyā”ti.
segs.e: That is how this spiritual path is lived supporting each other in order to cross over the flood and make a complete end of suffering.”
find success in the true teaching,

place faith in the perfected ones,

segs.p: “Ye keci, bhikkhave, bhikkhū kuhā thaddhā lapā siṅgī unnaḷā asamāhitā, na me te, bhikkhave, bhikkhū māmakā.
segs.e: “Mendicants, those mendicants who are deceivers and flatterers, pompous and fake, insolent and scattered: those mendicants are no followers of mine.

segs.p: Apagatā ca te, bhikkhave, bhikkhū imasmā dhammavinayā; na ca te imasmiṁ dhammavinaye vuddhiṁ virūḷhiṁ vepullaṁ āpajjanti.
segs.e: They’ve left this teaching and training, and they don’t achieve growth, improvement, or maturity in this teaching and training.

segs.p: Ye ca kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhū nikkuhā nillapā dhīrā atthaddhā susamāhitā, te kho me, bhikkhave, bhikkhū māmakā.
segs.e: But those mendicants who are genuine, not flatterers, attentive, amenable, and serene: those mendicants are followers of mine.

segs.p: Anapagatā ca te, bhikkhave, bhikkhū imasmā dhammavinayā; te ca imasmiṁ dhammavinaye vuddhiṁ virūḷhiṁ vepullaṁ āpajjantī”ti.
segs.e: They haven’t left this teaching and training, and they achieve growth, improvement, or maturity in this teaching and training.”
“Those who are deceivers and flatterers, <j>pompous and fake,
these don’t grow in the teaching
that was taught by the perfected Buddha.
But those who are genuine, not flatterers, attentive,
these do grow in the teaching
that was taught by the perfected Buddha.”

segs.p: “Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, puriso nadiyā sotena ovuyheyya piyarūpasātarūpena.
segs.e: “Suppose a person was being carried along by a river current that seemed nice and pleasant.

segs.p: Tamenaṁ cakkhumā puriso tīre ṭhito disvā evaṁ vadeyya:
segs.e: If a person with clear eyes saw them, they’d say:

segs.p: ‘kiñcāpi kho tvaṁ, ambho purisa, nadiyā sotena ovuyhasi piyarūpasātarūpena, atthi cettha heṭṭhā rahado saūmi sāvaṭṭo sagaho sarakkhaso yaṁ tvaṁ, ambho purisa, rahadaṁ pāpuṇitvā maraṇaṁ vā nigacchasi maraṇamattaṁ vā dukkhan’ti.
segs.e: ‘My man, even though the river current carrying you along seems nice and pleasant, downstream there is a lake with waves and whirlpools, saltwater crocodiles and monsters. When you reach there it will result in death or deadly pain.’

segs.p: Atha kho so, bhikkhave, puriso tassa purisassa saddaṁ sutvā hatthehi ca pādehi ca paṭisotaṁ vāyameyya.
segs.e: Then, when they heard what was said, they’d paddle against the stream using their hands and feet.

segs.p: Upamā kho me ayaṁ, bhikkhave, katā atthassa viññāpanāya.
segs.e: I’ve made up this simile to make a point.
‘River current’ is a term for craving.

segs.p: ‘Piyarūpaṁ sātarūpan’ti kho, bhikkhave, channetaṁ ajjhattikānaṁ āyatanānaṁ adhivacanaṁ.
segs.e: ‘Seeming nice and pleasant’ is a term for the six interior sense fields.

segs.p: ‘Heṭṭhā rahado’ti kho, bhikkhave, pañcannaṁ orambhāgiyānaṁ saṁyojanānaṁ adhivacanaṁ.
segs.e: ‘A downstream lake’ is a term for the five lower fetters.
‘Danger of waves’ is a term for anger and distress.
‘Whirlpool’ is a term for the five kinds of sensual stimulation.
‘Saltwater crocodiles and monsters’ is a term for ladies.
‘Against the stream’ is a term for renunciation.

segs.p: ‘Hatthehi ca pādehi ca vāyāmo’ti kho, bhikkhave, vīriyārambhassetaṁ adhivacanaṁ.
segs.e: ‘Paddling with hands and feet’ is a term for rousing energy.

segs.p: ‘Cakkhumā puriso tīre ṭhito’ti kho, bhikkhave, tathāgatassetaṁ adhivacanaṁ arahato sammāsambuddhassā”ti.
segs.e: ‘A person with clear eyes’ is a term for the Realized One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha.”
“In pain they’d give up sensual pleasures,
aspiring to the future sanctuary from the yoke.
With deep understanding and heart well freed,
That knowledge master <j>who has completed the spiritual journey,
and gone to the end of the world, <j>is called ‘one who has gone beyond’.”

segs.p: “Carato cepi, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno uppajjati kāmavitakko vā byāpādavitakko vā vihiṁsāvitakko vā.
segs.e: “Mendicants, suppose a mendicant has a sensual, malicious, or cruel thought while walking.

segs.p: Tañce, bhikkhave, bhikkhu adhivāseti nappajahati na vinodeti na byantīkaroti na anabhāvaṁ gameti.
segs.e: They tolerate it and don’t give it up, dispel it, eliminate it, and obliterate it. Such a mendicant is said to be ‘not keen or prudent, always lazy, and lacking energy’ when walking.

segs.p: Carampi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu evaṁbhūto anātāpī anottāpī satataṁ samitaṁ kusīto hīnavīriyoti vuccati.

Ṭhitopi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu evaṁbhūto anātāpī anottāpī satataṁ samitaṁ kusīto hīnavīriyoti vuccati.

segs.p: “Sampannasīlā, bhikkhave, viharatha sampannapātimokkhā; pātimokkhasaṁvarasaṁvutā viharatha ācāragocarasampannā aṇumattesu vajjesu bhayadassāvino; samādāya sikkhatha sikkhāpadesu.
segs.e: “Mendicants, live by the ethical precepts and the monastic code. Live restrained in the monastic code, conducting yourselves well and resorting for alms in suitable places. Seeing danger in the slightest fault, keep the rules you’ve undertaken.

segs.p: Sampannasīlānaṁ vo, bhikkhave, viharataṁ sampannapātimokkhānaṁ pātimokkhasaṁvarasaṁvutānaṁ viharataṁ ācāragocarasampannānaṁ aṇumattesu vajjesu bhayadassāvīnaṁ samādāya sikkhataṁ sikkhāpadesu, kimassa uttari karaṇīyaṁ?
segs.e: When you’ve done this, what more is there to do?

segs.p: Carato cepi, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno abhijjhā, byāpādo vigato hoti, thinamiddhaṁ vigataṁ hoti, uddhaccakukkuccaṁ vigataṁ hoti, vicikicchā pahīnā hoti, āraddhaṁ hoti vīriyaṁ asallīnaṁ, upaṭṭhitā sati asammuṭṭhā, passaddho kāyo asāraddho, samāhitaṁ cittaṁ ekaggaṁ.
segs.e: Suppose a mendicant has got rid of desire and ill will while walking, and has given up dullness and drowsiness, restlessness and remorse, and doubt. Their energy is roused up and unflagging, their mindfulness is established and lucid, their body is tranquil and undisturbed, and their mind is immersed and unified in samādhi.

segs.p: Carampi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu evaṁbhūto ātāpī ottāpī satataṁ samitaṁ āraddhavīriyo pahitattoti vuccati.
segs.e: Such a mendicant is said to be ‘keen and prudent, always energetic and resolute’ when walking.

segs.e: or when lying down while awake.

“Mendicants, the world has been understood by the Realized One;
and he is detached from the world.
The origin of the world has been understood by the Realized One;
and he has given up the origin of the world.
The cessation of the world has been understood by the Realized One;
and he has realized the cessation of the world.
The practice that leads to the cessation of the world has been understood by the Realized One;
and he has developed the practice that leads to the cessation of the world.

segs.p: Yaṁ, bhikkhave, sadevakassa lokassa samārakassa sabrahmakassa sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya diṭṭhaṁ sutaṁ mutaṁ viññātaṁ pattaṁ pariyesitaṁ anuvicaritaṁ manasā yasmā taṁ tathāgatena abhisambuddhaṁ,
segs.e: In this world—with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, its gods and humans—whatever is seen, heard, thought, known, attained, sought, and explored by the mind, all that has been understood by the Realized One.
That’s why he’s called the ‘Realized One’.

segs.p: Yañca, bhikkhave, rattiṁ tathāgato anuttaraṁ sammāsambodhiṁ abhisambujjhati, yañca rattiṁ anupādisesāya nibbānadhātuyā parinibbāyati, yaṁ etasmiṁ antare bhāsati lapati niddisati, sabbaṁ taṁ tatheva hoti no aññathā,
segs.e: From the night when the Realized One awakens to the supreme perfect awakening until the night he becomes fully extinguished—in the element of extinguishment with no residue—everything he speaks, says, and expresses is real, not otherwise.
That’s why he’s called the ‘Realized One’.

segs.p: Yathāvādī, bhikkhave, tathāgato tathākārī, yathākārī tathāvādī,
segs.e: The Realized One does as he says, and says as he does.
that’s why he’s called the ‘Realized One’.

segs.p: Sadevake, bhikkhave, loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya tathāgato abhibhū anabhibhūto aññadatthudaso vasavattī,
segs.e: In this world—with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, gods and humans—the Realized One is the vanquisher, the unvanquished, the universal seer, the wielder of power.
That’s why he’s called the ‘Realized One’.”

segs.p: Ayampi attho vutto bhagavatā, iti me sutanti.
segs.e: This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
